spec.title: vscode-extension PROP-004: Build, watch, lint, test, packaging and the preview

status.comment: the type's answers to the build question and to the preview question of PROP-016 §2, written 2026-11-01 from DESIGN-002 §2 and §3

p.VSX-PACKAGE-MANAGER: The family runs on four package managers and the type never guesses which: `typeConfig.packageManager` names it (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` or `bun`, default `npm`), the root manifest's `packageManager` field is checked against it at `check-tree` (PROP-002 `VSX-PACKAGE-MANAGER-FINGERPRINT`), and every command below is spelled for the declared one. A declared manager that is not installed on the host fails the command that first needs it, naming the manager; the type never installs one (DESIGN-002 D7, §6).

p.VSX-INSTALL: The install of the tree is the declared manager's frozen install at the tree root: `npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn install --immutable`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. A frozen install refuses to rewrite the lockfile, which is what makes it safe over a pinned tree.

p.VSX-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS: `node_modules` at the tree root is the dependency root; with `typeConfig.monorepo` the extension root's own `node_modules` is a second one, because a workspace install leaves the packages a root cannot hoist beside the package that needs them (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS`).

p.VSX-RUN-SCRIPT: A script of the extension manifest is run with the declared manager from the tree root, pointed at the extension root: `npm run <script> --workspace <extensionRoot>` (a repository that is one extension runs `npm run <script>`), `pnpm -C <extensionRoot> run <script>`, `yarn --cwd <extensionRoot> run <script>`, `bun run --cwd <extensionRoot> <script>`. The spelling is the type's; the engine spawns what it is handed and resolves `npm` alone to the platform's npm (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-BUILD`).

p.VSX-LINT: The hygiene gates are the scripts `typeConfig.scripts.lint` names, run in order through `VSX-RUN-SCRIPT`; the default is the one script `lint`, which the extension generator of the family writes into every manifest.

p.VSX-OWN-TESTS: The own tests are `typeConfig.scripts.test` - `{command, ownGlobArg?}` exactly as the `generic` type takes it, run over the glob `<ownRoot>/**/*.test.*` - or null when the patch set declares none: the family runs its unit tests through runners that differ per product, and a runner the type guessed would run the wrong suite silently.

p.VSX-BUILD-CHANNELS: The watch channels of the family are two, `bundle` and `typecheck`, both npm scripts of the extension manifest run through `VSX-RUN-SCRIPT`: `bundle` runs the bundler in watch mode (default script `watch:esbuild`; pass start `[watch] build started`, pass end `[watch] build finished`, the esbuild lines) and `typecheck` runs the compiler in watch mode (default script `watch:tsc`; the TypeScript watch lines, as the second family states them in `spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-004#THEIA-BUILD-CHANNELS`). A product whose scripts or bundler differ declares its channels in `typeConfig.watch.channels` with their pass boundaries, which replace the defaults whole; the boundaries are data the engine validates with the profile schema (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-010#PASS-BOUNDARIES-ARE-DATA`). Both channels are the default of a run that names none.

p.VSX-FOREIGN-WATCHER-MARKERS: Argv words that mean somebody else's watcher already runs over this tree: `esbuild --watch` and `tsc --watch`, the two commands the default channels start, so that two writers of `dist/` are refused as one too many.

p.VSX-PACKAGE-BUILD: `packageBuild` is one command, the script `typeConfig.scripts.build` (default `compile`) run through `VSX-RUN-SCRIPT`: the family's own build of the extension - type check, lint and bundle as the product's script composes them - into `dist/` of the extension root.

p.VSX-PACKAGE-DISTRIBUTABLE: `packageDistributable` is the script `typeConfig.scripts.package` run through `VSX-RUN-SCRIPT`, or empty when the patch set declares none. The distributable of the family is a `.vsix` written by `vsce package --no-dependencies`, and the product declares the script that runs it - in its manifest overlay, as `"vsix": "vsce package --no-dependencies -o dist/"` or whatever its packager needs - rather than the type spelling a `vsce` invocation (`DECISION-VSX-PACKAGE-SCRIPT-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`). `codkit package --skip-type-build` runs this half alone over a tree the watch channels already built (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`).

p.VSX-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS: `packageOutputs` is `<extensionRoot>/dist/*.vsix` by default, or the patterns `typeConfig.outputs` names; `codkit package` prints the ones that exist, and `preview` in the artifact mode installs the newest of them (`VSX-PREVIEW-ARTIFACT`). A packager that writes beside the tree names no output, as the contract says (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS-STAY-IN-THE-TREE`).

p.VSX-PACKAGE-SCRATCH: `packageScratch` is empty by default - neither the bundler nor `vsce package` edits a tracked file in place - plus the patterns `typeConfig.packageScratch` names for a product whose build script rewrites its manifest version or a generated file (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`).

p.VSX-STAMPS: `packageStamps` is empty by default: the family bakes neither a commit nor a date into the bundle. A product that reads a variable at build time declares it in `typeConfig.stamps` as `{name, value}` literals, which the type answers as literal stamps and the engine fills without overwriting what the operator exported (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP`).

p.DECISION-VSX-ONE-UNIVERSAL-VSIX: **Decision:** the first version answers one universal distributable through `packageBuild` and `packageDistributable` and no `packageTargets` catalog. **Why:** a `.vsix` of the extension's JavaScript is universal, and which platforms a product bundles native binaries for - the case that needs `vsce package --target` per platform - is the product's declaration, not the family's; the catalog of `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-TARGETS` is the right shape for it and arrives as `typeConfig.packageTargets` in a second version (campaign DEF-1). **Considered and rejected:** hard-coding the specimen's targets (a leak of one product into the family). **When to revisit:** the first `codkit package` of a product that ships native binaries.

p.DECISION-VSX-PACKAGE-SCRIPT-IS-THE-PRODU: **Decision:** the packaging command is a script of the product's manifest, declared in `typeConfig.scripts.package`, not a `vsce` invocation the type spells. **Why:** `vsce` must run in the extension root and reads the manifest there; a build command of the contract runs in the tree root with no working directory of its own, and the per-manager spelling of `VSX-RUN-SCRIPT` is exactly the mechanism that reaches the extension root; the second family made the same choice for its packager (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-004#THEIA-PACKAGE-BUILD`). **Considered and rejected:** running the `vsce` binary of `node_modules` through `node` (it would run in the tree root); a working directory on `BuildCommand` (a contract change for one command). **When to revisit:** a third family whose packager has no script to be named by.

p.VSX-PREVIEW-MODES: Two modes, `development` by default and `artifact`: the development host runs the extension from the loaded tree, the artifact mode installs the packaged `.vsix` into the isolated profile and opens the host on it. Both keep the person's own profile untouched (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PREVIEW-ISOLATION`).

p.VSX-PREVIEW-HOST: The default host of the family is the executable `code` - the command-line entry of Visual Studio Code, found on `PATH`; `typeConfig.preview.host` names another VS Code-based host - a path or a name - and the engine's resolution order puts the flag and the environment before it (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PREVIEW-HOST`). The custom editor of the owner's later step is one such value.

p.VSX-PREVIEW-DEVELOPMENT: The recipe of `development`: preparation is `packageBuild` (`VSX-PACKAGE-BUILD`), so the bundle the host loads is current; no artifact; the launch is the host with `--extensionDevelopmentPath=<treeDir>/<extensionRoot>`, `--user-data-dir <stateDir>/user-data`, `--extensions-dir <stateDir>/extensions`, `--new-window`, and the workspace folder when one is given; the two isolation directories are those two paths.

p.VSX-PREVIEW-ARTIFACT: The recipe of `artifact`: the distributable is needed, so the engine builds it first (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PREVIEW` step 5) and hands the newest match of `VSX-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS`; the preparation is one command, the host with `--install-extension <artifact>`, `--extensions-dir <stateDir>/extensions`, `--user-data-dir <stateDir>/user-data` and `--force`, which installs into the isolated profile and exits; the launch is the host with the same two directories, `--new-window` and the workspace folder when one is given.

p.VSX-PREVIEW-ISOLATION: Every launch and every preparation of both modes carries both isolation directories as whole arguments, under the state directory the engine hands over; a recipe of this type never names a directory under the person's home, and the engine's check of `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PREVIEW-ISOLATION` is what holds the promise when the type is wrong.
